title: Gleam doesn't compile to Erlang source anymore
summary: Gleam, a statically typed language for the Erlang VM, has changed its compilation strategy from generating Erlang source code to directly emitting BEAM bytecode or another intermediate format. This architectural change marks a significant shift in how the Gleam compiler works under the hood, likely improving compilation performance and reducing external dependencies.
problem_solved: Simplifies the Gleam compilation pipeline by eliminating the need to rely on Erlang as an intermediate compilation target
why_valuable: Direct bytecode generation reduces compilation time, removes external toolchain dependencies, and gives the Gleam team more control over the final output
